This is an [OkTrends](https://web.archive.org/web/20100310003658/http://blog.okcupid.com/) micro-post: weird, interesting, or provocative stuff that we've found in the online dating data mines.

Researching _[The Case For An Older Woman](https://web.archive.org/web/20100310003658/http://blog.okcupid.com/index.php/2010/02/16/the-case-for-an-older-woman/)_ we looked at outgoing messages sent by women of all ages. We found that young women don’t write much in response to an initial “hello” from a man. Older women do. It’s an interesting trend that I’ve depicted with lines:

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Of course, this makes sense when you think about the fact that Virginia Woolf and Pearl Buck _both_ were great writers and _both_ eventually became very old:

I’m just kidding. That has nothing to do with anything. Anyhow, what do you guys think is behind this trend? Message length levels off in the late twenties; is it a generational thing?
